best_for: Former Atom users, and anyone who wants a free editor they can reshape with JavaScript and CSS, without Microsoft or a company behind it.

points.title: Atom, kept alive
points.text: Pulsar is a community fork of the discontinued Atom editor, licensed MIT.

points.title: Packages and language servers
points.text: A built-in package manager finds and installs extensions. Language server support adds autocompletion and code navigation, and Git integration lets you stage changes, switch branches and resolve merge conflicts.

points.title: Expect a SmartScreen warning
points.text: Pulsar's Windows builds are not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen will warn you. Click More info, then Run anyway. A portable zip is also offered.

points.title: Minimum systems
points.text: The current release needs Windows 10 or later, macOS 10.15 Catalina or later, or a Linux system with glibc 2.31 or newer.

points.title: Linux: official packages first
points.text: The project ships .deb, .rpm, AppImage and tar.gz builds for x64 and Arm64. Flatpak is listed as community-supported, and the Flathub build is not marked verified. The AppImage may need libfuse2 on newer Ubuntu.

points.title: Separate Mac builds
points.text: macOS has its own DMGs for Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Once installed, the bundled updater tells you when a new release is out. Regular releases come about once a month.

points.title: Older versions
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 19 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release. Older builds for every system stay on the project's GitHub releases page.
